record.paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
record.context_brief: Time-dependent control in linear feedback networks
record.original_question: In linear feedback networks, how much performance improvement is obtained by adding time-dependent external control to systems and couplings that have usually been treated as time-independent, and how does the size of that improvement vary across different classes of quantum-control problems?

evidence.quote: So far work on linear feedback networks has been focussed on time-independent networks, in which the Hamiltonians of the systems and the couplings between then do not change with time. The analysis in [5] suggests that including time-dependence in networks can increase their performance for the purposes of control.
Problem 12: Quantify the increase in performance provided by including time-dependent external control in linear feedback networks, and examine how this varies across classes of problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear quantum feedback network: a collection of quantum systems whose internal dynamics are generated by quadratic Hamiltonians in canonical bosonic mode operators, interconnected through linear coupling channels (e.g., a cascaded or feedback configuration of input-output systems described by quantum stochastic differential equations of Hudson–Parthasarathy type). In the standard setting the system Hamiltonians H_k and the inter-system coupling operators L_{kj} are time-independent, and one optimizes a control performance functional J (for example, steady-state cooling, squeezing generation, state stabilization fidelity, entanglement production rate, or LQG-type cost) over the choice of these time-independent parameters.

Now allow each H_k(t) and each coupling L_{kj}(t) to depend on time, subject to the same physical admissibility constraints (e.g., quadratic in mode operators, bounded coupling strengths). Define the performance gap

  Δ(P) = sup_{time-dependent admissible networks} J(P) − sup_{time-independent admissible networks} J(P),

for a given class P of linear-feedback-network control problems.

(a) Quantify Δ(P): provide rigorous upper and lower bounds on the achievable improvement obtained by introducing time-dependent external control of the Hamiltonians and couplings, as a function of the network size, available control bandwidth, and the cost functional J.

(b) Determine how Δ(P) varies across natural classes P of such control problems (e.g., state preparation, dissipation engineering, parameter estimation, noise rejection, robust stabilization), identifying classes where time dependence yields strictly greater performance and, if any, classes where time-independent networks are optimal.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is one of the twenty open problems in quantum control posed in 2013. No specific resolution quantifying the performance gain from time-dependent control in linear quantum feedback networks across problem classes appears in the literature; while individual results show advantages of time-dependent coherent feedback in particular settings, a general quantification remains, to the best of available evidence, open.

status_evidence.snippet: List of twenty open problems including time-dependent linear feedback networks performance question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in the 2013 list and we found no source claiming its resolution.
